sprint: Sprint 7 — v0.3 Corpus Application and Standardization-Readiness Gate

BC-001.performance_window: From match start to the final whistle, including stoppage and any authorized extra time.

agency_segments.boundary_description: The governed match interval in which player actions change the result.
agency_segments.allowed_assistance: Declared equipment and lawful team coordination.
agency_segments.causal_attribution: Players and teams remain the primary causal performers.
agency_segments.uncertainty: No material phase ambiguity remains at this level of analysis.

distributed_arena_relation.physical_site_relation: Competing teams share one governed physical pitch.
distributed_arena_relation.synchronization_mechanism: Human and optional officiating systems share match time and event state.
distributed_arena_relation.latency_governance: Not a remote competition issue for the locked baseline object.
distributed_arena_relation.calibration_equivalence: Pitch and equipment conditions are governed by the Laws.
distributed_arena_relation.officiation_relation: Officials operate in the same contest environment.
distributed_arena_relation.safety_relation: One event safety authority governs the venue.
distributed_arena_relation.uncertainty: Optional technology deployments vary and do not create a remote distributed arena.

BC-002.performance_window: From the first legal move until checkmate, resignation, draw, forfeit, or time-based termination.

agency_segments.boundary_description: The move-and-clock sequence during which player decisions determine the result.
agency_segments.allowed_assistance: Standard interfaces and lawful assistance constraints.
agency_segments.causal_attribution: Human cognitive decisions remain causally necessary.
agency_segments.uncertainty: No material phase ambiguity remains at this level of analysis.

distributed_arena_relation.physical_site_relation: The activity may be over-the-board or online; the locked activity object does not select one deployment.
distributed_arena_relation.calibration_equivalence: Time control and platform conditions are deployment-specific.
distributed_arena_relation.safety_relation: Not material to category classification in this record.
distributed_arena_relation.uncertainty: A product- or event-locked record is required for a stronger arena relation.

BC-003.performance_window: From the race start procedure through classified finish or retirement.

agency_segments.boundary_description: The timed race interval during which the driver controls the car.
agency_segments.allowed_assistance: Regulated vehicle systems, lawful controls, and team information.
agency_segments.causal_attribution: Driver execution is causally necessary while engineering and strategy co-determine competitive capacity.
agency_segments.uncertainty: No material phase ambiguity remains at this level of analysis.

distributed_arena_relation.physical_site_relation: Drivers compete on one physical circuit while teams and control functions occupy coordinated venue zones.
distributed_arena_relation.synchronization_mechanism: Timing, marshalling, telemetry, and race-control systems synchronize contest state.
distributed_arena_relation.latency_governance: Communications and telemetry matter operationally but do not create remote athletic performance.
distributed_arena_relation.calibration_equivalence: Technical regulations and timing systems define comparison conditions.
distributed_arena_relation.officiation_relation: Race control and stewards govern the shared event.
distributed_arena_relation.safety_relation: Circuit-wide safety responsibility is centrally governed.
distributed_arena_relation.uncertainty: This is a co-located event relation, not a remote synchronous athletic arena.

participatory_actor_relations.action_window: During authorized team communications and strategy windows.
participatory_actor_relations.mechanism: Team radio and pit-wall analysis provide information to the driver.
participatory_actor_relations.resource_or_constraint_effect: Information may alter strategy or resource use, but the engineer does not execute vehicle control.
participatory_actor_relations.uncertainty: The exact causal weight of team information varies by event phase.

BC-004.performance_window: The governed event interval from authorized start through measured completion.

agency_segments.boundary_description: The event interval in which the athlete performs within classification and equipment rules.
agency_segments.allowed_assistance: Adaptive or assistive equipment permitted by class and event rules.
agency_segments.causal_attribution: Athlete performance remains causally necessary within the governed class.
agency_segments.uncertainty: No material phase ambiguity remains at this level of analysis.

distributed_arena_relation.physical_site_relation: Athletes share a governed track or field event site.
distributed_arena_relation.synchronization_mechanism: Timing, measurement, and officiating systems coordinate event state.
distributed_arena_relation.latency_governance: Not a remote synchronous issue for the locked case.
distributed_arena_relation.calibration_equivalence: Classification, equipment, and measurement controls support comparison.
distributed_arena_relation.officiation_relation: Officials and classification governance apply to the event.
distributed_arena_relation.safety_relation: Venue and event safety responsibility is defined.
distributed_arena_relation.uncertainty: Future hybrid para events require separate records.

BC-005.performance_window: From race start through course completion, disqualification, or loss of controlled flight.

agency_segments.boundary_description: The race interval in which the pilot controls the aircraft through radio and FPV.
agency_segments.allowed_assistance: Regulated radio control, FPV display, and aircraft systems.
agency_segments.causal_attribution: Pilot control, line choice, and risk management are causally necessary.
agency_segments.uncertainty: The pilot and aircraft are spatially separated, but the degree of computational arena constitution remains disputed.

distributed_arena_relation.physical_site_relation: The pilot operates from a protected control position while the aircraft traverses a separate physical course.
distributed_arena_relation.synchronization_mechanism: Radio command, FPV video, timing, and course state connect pilot and aircraft.
distributed_arena_relation.latency_governance: Video and control-link latency are material but event-specific.
distributed_arena_relation.calibration_equivalence: Equipment classes, frequencies, timing, and course configuration bound comparison.
distributed_arena_relation.officiation_relation: Officials observe the physical course and results systems.
distributed_arena_relation.safety_relation: Pilot zones, spectator separation, frequency control, and flyaway procedures govern risk.
distributed_arena_relation.uncertainty: Remote control of a physical craft is represented; this does not by itself prove a computationally constituted arena.

BC-006.performance_window: From round start through the governed end condition of each match.

agency_segments.boundary_description: The round and match intervals in which player input changes authoritative game state.
agency_segments.allowed_assistance: Approved hardware, software, communications, and tournament settings.
agency_segments.causal_attribution: Player aim, tactics, coordination, and decisions are causally necessary.
agency_segments.uncertainty: No material phase ambiguity remains at this level of analysis.

distributed_arena_relation.physical_site_relation: Tournament deployments may be LAN, co-located, or online; the activity-cluster object does not fix one physical topology.
distributed_arena_relation.synchronization_mechanism: The authoritative game server synchronizes computational contest state.
distributed_arena_relation.latency_governance: Tournament-specific network and server rules govern latency.
distributed_arena_relation.calibration_equivalence: Patch, hardware, settings, and anti-cheat controls are event-specific.
distributed_arena_relation.officiation_relation: Game code and tournament administrators share authority.
distributed_arena_relation.safety_relation: Physical-site and online participation risks differ by deployment.
distributed_arena_relation.uncertainty: A locked event record is required before selecting co-located or remote-synchronous topology.

BC-007.performance_window: The active session or governed PvP match interval during which tracked actions affect game state.

agency_segments.boundary_description: The session interval in which tracked upper-body actions produce in-game attacks and defense.
agency_segments.allowed_assistance: Headset, controllers, tracking, and product-defined assistance.
agency_segments.causal_attribution: Player timing and movement are causally necessary at the product configuration examined.
agency_segments.uncertainty: No material phase ambiguity remains at this level of analysis.

distributed_arena_relation.physical_site_relation: The product family may support local or remote PvP; the locked product-centered hybrid does not establish a single governed topology.
distributed_arena_relation.latency_governance: Not sufficiently evidenced for a general claim.
distributed_arena_relation.officiation_relation: Software resolves events; formal contest authority is weak or mode-specific.
distributed_arena_relation.safety_relation: Each participant's physical play space has local safety constraints.
distributed_arena_relation.uncertainty: A specific league or event configuration is required.

BC-008.performance_window: From race start through classified finish in the governed virtual cycling event.

agency_segments.boundary_description: The synchronized race interval in which rider power, tactics, and platform state determine outcome.
agency_segments.allowed_assistance: Smart trainers, regulated sensors, platform physics, and declared equipment controls.
agency_segments.causal_attribution: Human physiological and tactical performance remains causally necessary.
agency_segments.uncertainty: No material phase ambiguity remains at this level of analysis.

distributed_arena_relation.physical_site_relation: Riders occupy separate physical sites while sharing one computational race state.
distributed_arena_relation.synchronization_mechanism: Platform position, course state, power input, and event timing synchronize the race.
distributed_arena_relation.latency_governance: Network conditions are material and require event governance, even where public detail is incomplete.
distributed_arena_relation.calibration_equivalence: Trainer standardization, power-source rules, and sensor controls support equivalence.
distributed_arena_relation.officiation_relation: Platform state and event officials jointly administer the race.
distributed_arena_relation.safety_relation: Each rider's local physical setup remains locally managed while contest governance is centralized.
distributed_arena_relation.uncertainty: Public evidence supports remote distributed participation, but detailed network tolerances may remain non-public.

BC-009.performance_window: The defined simulated flight task, race, or contest interval.

agency_segments.boundary_description: The contest interval in which human control changes simulated aircraft state.
agency_segments.allowed_assistance: Simulation controls and any declared motion or assistance systems.
agency_segments.causal_attribution: Human piloting skill is causally necessary in the contest configurations examined.
agency_segments.uncertainty: No material phase ambiguity remains at this level of analysis.

distributed_arena_relation.physical_site_relation: The hybrid case includes product contests and network operations with different topologies.
distributed_arena_relation.synchronization_mechanism: Simulator or network state can be shared computationally.
distributed_arena_relation.calibration_equivalence: Hardware and software variance remain material.
distributed_arena_relation.officiation_relation: Publisher, software, or community administration varies by contest.
distributed_arena_relation.safety_relation: Physical consequences are limited; local setup and fatigue remain relevant.
distributed_arena_relation.uncertainty: Object heterogeneity prevents one arena relation from representing every flight-simulation use.

BC-010.performance_window: The complete governed contest lifecycle, with pre-match engineering separated from autonomous match execution.

agency_segments.boundary_description: Before the match, human teams design, train, configure, and prepare the robots.
agency_segments.allowed_assistance: Permitted software, hardware, and training processes.
agency_segments.causal_attribution: Human engineering determines system capability but is not live athletic performance.
agency_segments.uncertainty: Team development processes differ and may not be fully public.

agency_segments.boundary_description: During governed play, robots sense, decide, and act without teleoperation.
agency_segments.transition_trigger: match start or release to autonomous play
agency_segments.allowed_assistance: Only rule-permitted handler interventions and service exceptions.
agency_segments.causal_attribution: Robots are the executing agents during the match; human design remains prior causal contribution.
agency_segments.uncertainty: Internal autonomy architectures vary by team.

distributed_arena_relation.physical_site_relation: Robots compete on one physical field while human teams remain outside direct live control.
distributed_arena_relation.synchronization_mechanism: Onboard sensing and game-control systems coordinate match state.
distributed_arena_relation.latency_governance: No remote human performance claim is made.
distributed_arena_relation.calibration_equivalence: Technical and league rules bound platform conditions.
distributed_arena_relation.officiation_relation: Human referees and game controllers govern the field.
distributed_arena_relation.safety_relation: Robot and human safety procedures apply at the venue.
distributed_arena_relation.uncertainty: Computational perception is extensive but does not create human athletic agency.
